Olivia

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@optixai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OptixAI renewal + mid-term GPU add — need options

Thanks Olivia — appreciate the visibility and the CSV. Quick summary of feasible approaches and tradeoffs: 

Option A — Mid-term top-up (fastest)
- Add N GPUs into your existing pool immediately as a burst/top-up.
- Pricing: one-off charge at standard top-up rate (no change to committed discount tier).
- Pros: immediate capacity, minimal operational change.
- Cons: no retroactive increase to committed discount; top-ups are billed at slightly higher rate than committed units.

Option B — Mid-term commit uplift (recommended for sustained growth)
- Convert a portion of top-up to reserved commits for the remainder of your term (pro-rated).
- Pricing: pro-rated commit price + partial adjustment of previous discount tier.
- Pros: preserves lower unit economics going forward, eligible for higher SLA and guaranteed throughput.
- Cons: requires amendment and procurement sign-off.

Option C — Wait to combine with renewal (simpler contracting)
- Resize pool at renewal and lock a higher commit tier for 12/24 months.
- Pros: best long-term price; simpler paperwork once.
- Cons: risk of immediate capacity shortfall.

Throughput guarantees: we can commit to p95 latency SLOs for steady-state requests and provide p99 targets in the commitment if you place those added GPUs into a reserved commit (Option B or C). For mid-term top-up (Option A) we provide best-effort routing with burst capacity but cannot include p99 backed credits.

I've attached a draft proposal and a capacity workbook so you can model cost/throughput. I'll loop in Rishi and Lauren for discounts and contracting cadence.

Attachments: 20280315-OptixAI-dedicated-proposal.pdf; optix-capacity-workbook-2028-03.xlsx

Next step: tell me which option you prefer and the target effective date (immediate vs renewal). If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call this week to run numbers with your infra team.

—Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Questions for Rishi / Lauren:
- Can we offer a pro-rated commit uplift that converts 60% of the requested GPUs into reserved commits for the remaining 9 months of their term? What discount delta should we apply?
- If procurement wants immediate capacity and then converts to commit within 30 days, can we provide a temporary price hold for that window?

Notes: OptixAI cares about guaranteed throughput for A/B tests during rollout; p99 backed in contract is a must for them.

-Marcus
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: OptixAI renewal + mid-term GPU add — recommended approach

Thanks Marcus. Pricing playbook suggestions below — conservative but competitive. All numbers are per-GPU equivalent (normalized):

- Baseline (current commit): 100 units at Tier 2 (12-month) — effective unit rate: $1.00/tokenized-unit
- Mid-term top-up (Option A): top-up premium = +12% on baseline per-unit rate (no change to tier).
- Pro-rated commit uplift (Option B): convert portion to reserved commit pro-rated over remaining term. Discount delta: offer an incremental 8–12% off top-up price depending on conversion percentage (60% => 11%).
- Renewal bundle (Option C): if they sign a 12-month uplift that includes +40 GPUs starting at renewal we can offer 18% off baseline for the new committed units; 24-month commit => 22% off.

Operational asks to enable p99 guarantee:
- Place committed GPUs in a segregated pool to isolate noisy neighbors (we can do this with dedicated placement).
- Enable request-level priority queues and optional throttling for non-critical routes.

Temporary price hold: we can do a 30-day hold if procurement commits to a PO within that window and a contract amendment is executed within 45 days.

I'll draft the amendment language for the pro-rated uplift and the temporary price hold. Recommend we present 2 guided scenarios to Optix: (1) immediate +30-day hold -> convert 60% to commit (fast), (2) wait and combine at renewal for best rate.

-Rishi

Marcus / Rishi — thanks for the quick turn. OptixAI prefers Option B with the following parameters:

- Immediate add of +40 GPUs on a 30-day temporary hold (we need capacity tomorrow for the rollout).
- Convert 60% (24 GPUs) to reserved commit pro-rated over the remaining 9 months of our term.
- Apply the 11% uplift discount as discussed for the converted units.
- Include p99-backed throughput guarantee for the 24 reserved GPUs and segregated placement.

Procurement will prepare a PO by Mar 20. Please send the proposed amendment and DocuSign link for signatures. Also include the final quote PDF and the capacity workbook you shared earlier.

Olivia Park
Director, Platform Engineering, OptixAI
